note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after c41ebbaf93 moved the esp-group existence check from the deleted ValidateGroupRefs to the YANG leafref the commit path runs. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 re-read in rfc/full/rfc4301.txt: "SPD-S: For traffic that is to be protected using IPsec, the entry consists of the values of the selectors that apply to the traffic to be protected via AH or ESP, controls on how to create SAs based on these selectors, and the parameters needed to effect this protection (e.g., algorithms, modes, etc.)." Q1 both units assert the three parts of the entry, which is what the RFC says. Q2 TestRFC4301SPDSEntryCarriesSelectorsSAControlsAndProtection parses one site-to-site peer through ParseIPsecConfig, requires config.ValidateCustomSections (referenceRefusals) to raise no esp-group/name refusal, and reads back the selector prefixes, the SA creation controls (connection-type, remote address, esp-group) and the protection parameters (mode transport, aes256/sha256), each compared exactly; TestRFC4301SPDSEntryRefusesAMissingOrUnusablePart breaks one part per case (undefined esp-group now refused by the leafref with 'no name "absent" exists at "../../../esp-group/name"', mode beet, unknown connection-type, a /33 selector) and requires a refusal naming that part. Revert records on config.go::parseSiteToSitePeer verify for both polarities. Q3 each negative case changes one leaf of an otherwise complete entry. Q4 all three parts of the entry are covered. The change replaced the producer of one refusal and kept every input and expected part, so the verdict stays enforced.
